details.description: GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's frontier coding and agentic model, built on the same base as GLM-5.2 with all of its gains coming from further post-training rather than a new base model. It is a 753-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that always reasons, with three selectable thinking-effort levels (low, high, max), and supports a 1M-token context window with function calling, context caching and structured JSON output. Z.ai reports large gains over GLM-5.2 on long, multi-day agentic coding tasks and on security-research benchmarks such as vulnerability discovery. It is text-only and is generally available to Z.ai's GLM Coding Plan subscribers.
advantages: Scores 84.5% on the CyberGym vulnerability-discovery benchmark, per Z.ai's documentation.
Improves from 4.6 to 28.3 on Terminal-Bench 3.0 versus GLM-5.2, per Z.ai's documentation.
More than doubles GLM-5.2's score on ExploitBench, reaching 54.4%, per Z.ai's documentation.
Reports a 50% improvement over GLM-5.2 on Z.ai's in-house Code Bench, reaching 34.5% at max thinking effort.
Supports a 1M-token context window with function calling, context caching and structured JSON output, per Z.ai's documentation.
disadvantages: Text-only input; does not accept image, video or other multimodal input, unlike the GLM-5.3-Flash variant.
Reasoning is always on and cannot be disabled; Z.ai says apps that previously used a disabled-thinking setting must be migrated.
use_cases: Frontier agentic coding, including multi-day, end-to-end engineering tasks
Security research: vulnerability discovery and exploit development
General reasoning and chat with adjustable thinking effort

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens (1,048,575) and max_output_tokens (128,000) match Z.ai's own docs (1M context / 128K output) exactly, and the catalog's text-only modality matches Z.ai's docs, which state GLM-5.3 accepts text-only input (vision is on the separate GLM-5.3-Flash model).
